Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

subject noun

a topic

also topic, theme, subject matter, back to the subject

classical

Plin. Ep. 9.33.1: incidī in māteriam vēram
Phaedr. 1 prol. 1
Traupman 32, 387

māteria, māteriae f.

noun, first declension

subject matter, a subject to talk or write about

Lewis & Short: the matter, subject, topic, theme of any work of the mind; properly timber, building material.

Other words

  • argūmentum, argūmentī n. — the subject or plot of a play, a story or a letter

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 9.10.1: nūllō argūmentō prōpositō; Quint. 5.10.9 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 32; M-O s.v. subject (topic)

  • thema, thematis n. — a theme set for a speech or an essay

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Quint. 4.2.28 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. subject (topic)

    Greek θέμα; post-Augustan, in the schools of declamation (Seneca the Elder, Quintilian).

Examples

  • incidī in māteriam vēram sed simillimam fictae

    I’ve come across a subject that is true, but very like fictionPlin. Ep. 9.33.1

  • sed redeō ad Plīnium

    but to get back to PlinyGell. 10.12.4

See also subject, issue, story.

SourcesLewis & Short: materia · Lewis & Short: argumentum · Lewis & Short: thema

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. subject (topic).
